slides.texto_narrado: How much do you actually let your *five-year-old* do out here — before deciding for them that they can't?
At five, they *can* read a seed packet and plant exactly what it says — that's not luck, that's a kindergarten skill already at work.
They *can* water a seedling tray without drowning it. Small can, slow pour — five-year-old hands are plenty steady for that.
They *can* pick the low fruit clean off the vine. What they *can't* do yet is the pruning shears — that one's still yours.
Not because they're not capable — because sharp tools and five-year-olds need an adult hand right there, every time.
Know the line between ready and not-yet-ready. Age-by-age garden guide, link in bio.// So how much do you actually let them do?
